The closest match to “Wei complexity structural generalization” is Zichao Wei’s paper “On the Computational Complexity of Structural Generalization.” It argues that structural generalization can be framed as a computational-complexity tension between an NC^1 lower bound (via a tree-evaluation component described as BFVP, NC^1-complete) and the learned ceiling of pure Transformers being within TC^0; under the assumption TC^0 ≠ NC^1, a pure Transformer cannot learn structural generalization. It also claims that neuro-symbolic systems score well by injecting part of the structure, rather than learning the hard component from finite data. [1]

Wei also studies structural generalization operationally in “Structural Generalization on SLOG without Hand-Written Rules,” using a neural cellular automaton with a discrete bottleneck to learn compositional rules from data and analyzing where failures concentrate on specific structural mechanisms. [2]

These two Wei papers differ: [1] is a computational complexity/theory argument about what pure Transformers can learn, while [2] is an empirical/diagnostic study of structural generalization on SLOG without hand-written rules.
